title: Claudia’s Strong Army, Which Backs the Fourth Transformation
author: Pedro Mellado Rodríguez
content:
_This article by[Pedro Mellado
Rodríguez](https://www.sinembargo.mx/author/pedromellado/) originally appeared
in the [November 13, 2026 edition of
SinEmbargo](https://www.sinembargo.mx/4903132/el-fuerte-ejercito-de-claudia-
que-respalda-a-la-4t/), a Mexican digital news outlet._

_Photo: Cuartoscuro, enhanced with artificial intelligence._

_“It will be very difficult for this majority of the poor, the helpless, the
discriminated against, the abandoned, to stop backing the government of the
Fourth Transformation.”_

They are quiet, silent, unhurried, and they will be the first at the polls in
the elections on Sunday, June 6, 2027, to cast their votes. They will arrive
on their own or with the support of their children or grandchildren. They are
Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo’s army that backs the government of the Fourth
Transformation and will carry it to victory, giving the President of the
Republic a majority in the federal Chamber of Deputies and in a large share of
the state congresses whose legislatures will be renewed.

The Nominal List of Voters, updated by the National Electoral Institute (INE)
as of Thursday, October 29, 2026, includes just over 101 million people with
valid voter ID cards and reflects a very significant and impressive fact that
had not been seen in the last eight years: by far, people aged 60 and older
now represent the largest segment of those eligible to go to the polls in the
elections on the first Sunday of June 2027, as they exceed 20 million
citizens.

It should be recalled that older voters posted the most notable turnout
figures in the elections held on Sunday, June 2, 2024: citizens aged 60 to 74
had an **average turnout of 75 percent** , above the 72 percent recorded in
2018. The hard data show that in the 2018 elections older adults represented
16.55 percent of the Nominal List of Voters, and by October 2026 they
accounted for 20.65 percent.

The Sample Study of Citizen Participation in the 2023-2024 Concurrent
Electoral Process, published by the National Electoral Institute’s Electoral
Organization Commission on Monday, December 9, 2024, allows us to observe an
increase of more than 4 million citizens in the older adult segment, compared
with 2018, in the Nominal List of Voters as of Thursday, October 29, 2026.

In January 2018, when Andrés Manuel López Obrador became President of the
Republic, the Nominal List of Voters included more than 87 million people, and
there were just over 14.5 million older citizens with voter ID cards. In
October 2026, that segment already totals **more than 20.6 million people**.
This is very bad news for the opposition of all stripes and colors, as older
adults have a particular preference for Morena, ever since López Obrador
committed to giving priority in his government to the poorest people through
well-being pensions.

The study of citizen participation in the 2024 elections, when the Nominal
List of Voters included just over 98 million people, also concludes that there
was a noticeable decline in young voter turnout between 2018 and 2024. Young
people voting for the first time in 2018 had a participation rate of 64.7
percent, while in 2024 that percentage fell to 61.6 percent. It is also
important to observe that abstention increased among voters aged 20 to 29, as
only 48 percent of the citizens registered on the Nominal List of Voters went
to the polls.

These two age segments, those aged 20 to 24 and those aged 25 to 29, are the
largest after older adults. In 2018, together they represented 24.86 percent
of the votes, compared with the 22.26 percent they total in 2026. This
potential electoral force is not decisive at the polls, since while older
adults turn out to vote at a rate of 75 percent, only 48 percent of young
people go to cast their ballots.

It should also be kept in mind that in the 2024 elections women had a higher
turnout than men, at 64.3 percent, a figure 9.5 percentage points above men’s
turnout of 54.8 percent. In the current Nominal List of Voters, 52.03 percent
are women and 47.96 percent are men. There are four percent more women who
could go to vote next year.

The third-largest age segment among potential voters heading toward the June
2027 elections is people aged 30 to 34, who totaled 9.5 million citizens in
2018 and more than 10.7 million with voter ID cards in October 2026. However,
the INE’s 2024 Sample Study of Citizen Participation reveals that between the
2018 and 2024 elections, this age segment’s average electoral turnout fell
from 58.1 percent to 52.1 percent.

## Well-Being Pensions

In the last four decades, from the PRI administration of Miguel de la Madrid
Hurtado to that of Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo, no government had devoted so many
resources to well-being pensions for the benefit of those most in need, which
by the end of 2026 will directly affect **more than 42.8 million people**
throughout the country, according to an estimate from the Secretariat of Well-
being, assessed on October 23, 2026.

As of the end of October, the Single Register of Beneficiaries of well-being
programs included **13.8 million people receiving the Pension for Older
Adults**. Another program with broad coverage is the Rita Cetina Scholarship,
which, according to an October 11, 2026 report from the Secretariat of
Education, serves 14.9 million children in preschool, primary and lower
secondary education.

Add to this that the Benito Juárez Scholarship, which supports students in
upper secondary education, assists 3.9 million young people; the Mujeres
Bienestar pension totals 2.8 million people, in addition to programs with
smaller enrollment such as Sembrando Vida, La Escuela es Nuestra, Salud Casa
por Casa, Jóvenes Escribiendo el Futuro, the Pension for People With Permanent
Disabilities, as well as the various initiatives supporting orphaned children,
farmworkers and fishers.

After decades of neglect, of administrations that never cared about them, it
will be very difficult for this majority of the poor, the helpless, the
discriminated against, the abandoned, to stop backing the government of the
Fourth Transformation, which allocated **one trillion pesos (one million
million pesos)** to them in 2026, the same budget approved in the 2027 federal
spending plan by the federal Chamber of Deputies last Tuesday, November 10,
2026.

The importance of programs supporting people’s well-being under the current
federal government is reflected in the concrete fact that in 2027 they will
represent 10 percent of the entire Federal Expenditure Budget, which totals 10
trillion pesos, that is, 10 million million pesos. All of this will motivate
older people to be at the front of the voting lines in June 2027.
